subject: Taxes
title: Taxes on Investments
description: A fast breakdown of Taxes on Investments for builders.

hook.text: Investment profits are taxed, but only when you sell. Unrealized gains—paper profits—aren't taxed.

buildup.text: If you buy stock for $10,000 and it grows to $1 million, you owe zero tax until you sell.

discovery.text: This is called the 'buy, borrow, die' strategy. Billionaires hold assets, borrow against them.

twist.text: When the investor dies, heirs receive a 'stepped-up basis': the original gain is erased.

climax.text: Unrealized gains and stepped-up basis are the two biggest legal tax advantages for the ultra-wealthy.

punchline.text: Buy, borrow, die. The billionaire tax avoidance playbook.

quiz.question: What is 'stepped-up basis'?
options: Erasing unrealized gains when assets pass to heirs
A higher tax rate for investors
